title: Epochal ring schism with lazy KV handshake to increase comm/compute overlap for TP workloads
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Tensor-parallel training/inference exhibits periods where NCCL ring progress stalls waiting on KV cache eviction and kernel readiness. This PR introduces an epochal ring ‘schism’ allocator plus a lazy KV handshake protocol to allow NCCL collectives to proceed opportunistically while KV cache eviction and slot reclamation complete asynchronously. The goal is to improve overlap of comm/compute in multi-GPU TP serving scenarios without increasing peak memory footprint.

Design summary: single-coherent change implemented in three parts: 1) epochal ring allocator: rings are versioned (epoch IDs) so peers can progress on a sovled subset of rings while others drain; 2) NCCL handoff path changes: lightweight per-ring state machine and a short-lived fallback ring to preserve forward progress when peers lag; 3) lazy KV handshake: on eviction path we introduce a two-phase handshake where eviction requests mark slots as reclaimable immediately while the actual data scrubbing runs asynchronously; requesters may speculatively launch collectives that only require reclaim-marked slots.

Why unique: differs from previous ‘staggered’ and ‘pipelined’ schedulers by versioning ring topology at runtime and decoupling KV slot lifetime from immediate data deletion — this reduces critical-path stalls and helps the kernel scheduler keep GPU SMs busy.

Performance: internal canary on a 16xA800 TP model (seq_len=2048, microbatch=8) shows median tail latency improvement of 18% and 99th percentile wall time improvement of 22% for end-to-end generation under sustained load. Throughput increased ~9% at 95th percentile. Memory overhead: <2% peak GPU memory increase due to short-lived fallback rings.

Testing & safety: added unit tests for ring epoch transitions, simulated multi-node integration test that injects artificial delays on one peer, and extended kvcache evictions tests to assert no double-free races. CI ran GPU-integration suite; an intermittent kernel-torch binding flake surfaced and was fixed in a follow-up commit.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag TP_ENABLE_EPOCHAL_RING (off by default). Canary rollout on Dedicated capacity clusters for a week, monitor per-route tail-latency and kvcache drop rates. If metrics regress >5% in tail latency we will auto-disable and rollback.

Files of interest: runtime/scheduler/epochal_ring_allocator.cc, runtime/collectives/nccl_handoff.h/.cc, runtime/kvcache/lazy_handshake.{h,cc}, tests/integration/tp_epochal_ring_sim.py, docs/rfc/epochal-ring-kv-handshake.md.

Checklist: [x] design doc + perf numbers [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] gated runtime flag [x] metrics dashboard slice

Related: builds on ENG-1842 (comm/compute overlap initiative) and complements PRs that adjust kernel microbatching.
